News Sites Are Fatter and Slower Than Ever

This is fascinating. I can definitely see this being true. I was a frustrated journalism major once who was told the school could teach me to "talk to engineers" for web design projects. In general, I think the media is still fighting change, wanting to stay with the simpler formats of paper, radio and TV. They don't put as much emphasis on the web, and they seriously should.

I have friends who are still journalism majors, and they become so proud when their story goes on an "actual" publication. The web is a punishment to them. Something needs to change.
Seeing their work on the web as punishment is asking for redundancy if you ask me.

Bloated sites often mean I use a mobilizer rather than viewing on the site itself. I'm not going to wait for 30s for it to load just so they get their fractional pennies from ads, I'm going to use a mobilizer.

IMO the main problem is that effort and resources are put into aesthetics and business rather than content. As a result it becomes more and more difficult to find trustable content and I spend more and more time fact-checking, basically doing the job that should have been done by the author/publisher.

Washington would be wise to give Holtby damn near anything he asks for and be done with it. He's only going to get better as a goalie and I image he'll hoist a Stanley Cup. It's up to Washington if he does that with them or not.

If Holtby is really only asking for $6mil to counter their $5mil offer the Caps would be absolutely foolish to let this go to arbitration. I know we've had a great track record of cranking out good to great goalies over the past decade or so, but you don't let a guy of Holtby's skill and age get away.

It always comes back to alternatives. What can the Caps do without Holtby? Who do they have in the pipeline, who's their backup, and are they better than Holtby next year? When it comes down to it, giving him the $6 mil is cheap if it gets them wins.
